items.name: Little Venice
items.description: A magical network of canals with painted houseboats, waterside cafes and peaceful towpaths. Few tourists ever discover this peaceful corner of London.

items.name: Kyoto Garden
items.description: A perfectly manicured Japanese garden hidden inside Holland Park with waterfalls, koi carp and peacocks. Completely free and almost always quiet.

items.name: Leadenhall Market
items.description: A stunning Victorian covered market that inspired Diagon Alley in Harry Potter. Gorgeous architecture, great bars and restaurants hidden in the City.

items.name: God's Own Junkyard
items.description: A mind-blowing warehouse filled floor to ceiling with vintage neon signs and pop art. A photographer's dream and one of London's most unique spaces.

items.name: Postman's Park
items.description: A tiny park near St Paul's with a Victorian memorial wall dedicated to ordinary people who died saving others. Incredibly moving and almost always empty.

items.name: Bermondsey Street
items.description: One of London's most characterful streets with independent restaurants, boutiques, the White Cube gallery and easy walk to Tower Bridge. Locals love it.

items.name: Crossbones Garden
items.description: A hidden memorial garden on an ancient burial ground decorated with ribbons, flowers and messages. Hauntingly beautiful and completely unknown to most visitors.

items.name: Neal's Yard
items.description: A tiny, colourful courtyard hidden off Seven Dials in Covent Garden. Bright painted buildings, wholefood cafes and an alternative vibe that surprises everyone.
